label: risky
summary: pull_request_target workflow checks out and runs untrusted PR code with a write-all token and a secret (a 'pwn request').

findings.title: Untrusted pull request code runs in a privileged pull_request_target job
findings.description: The workflow is triggered by pull_request_target, which runs with the base repository's secrets and token, then checks out the pull request head and runs npm ci and a build script from it. A fork PR can execute arbitrary code with PREVIEW_DEPLOY_KEY and a write token.
findings.recommendation: Use the pull_request trigger for building untrusted code, or split the job so the privileged part never checks out or runs PR code.

evidence.observation: Workflow runs on pull_request_target, including for fork PRs.
Checks out the untrusted pull request head commit.
Runs install and build scripts from the checked-out PR code with a secret in the environment.

findings.title: Workflow grants write-all token permissions
findings.description: permissions: write-all gives the GITHUB_TOKEN write access to every scope, far more than a preview build needs.
findings.recommendation: Set permissions to the minimum required, for example contents: read, and grant extra scopes per job.
uncertainty: Did not check repository-level default token permissions.
